question: at a fixed pool, capacity, schedule and step budget, does rotating CUT cells help or hurt?
why_open: every multi-seat cut arm ran --augment --augment-full-only, which leaves cut cells in the identity frame: augmented_seats was 0 of 32 (cutonly_noaug), 0 of 73 (wide_cut), 0 for ncut_02/04/08/16/59, and 28 of 64 for cutmix_fullaug where the 28 are its box seats.  The only contrary evidence is the n=1 pair solo_100079 / noaug_100079.
train_pool_source: the in-domain subset of CUTONLY_NOAUG's 28 cut seats, so DOSE_00 is that configuration restricted to tau_mean <= 0.45
dropped_reason: tau_mean > 0.45, outside the design domain the optimiser works

arms.name: DOSE_00
arms.note: identical code path to every historical cut arm: cut cells stay in the identity frame

arms.name: DOSE_00B
arms.note: SEED CONTROL.  Its distance from DOSE_00 is the resolution of this experiment; any dose difference smaller than that is not a finding

arms.name: DOSE_24
arms.note: the 24 proper rotations reach the cut cells

arms.name: DOSE_48
arms.note: all 48, so improper elements and the z-tilted planes the dataset does not contain

metric.primary: median over the 12 held-out seats of each seat median absolute face-load response error, assembly-free, on the final checkpoint, via sweep_checkpoints
secondary: the presented seat 100032 for the presented-to-held-out gap

decision_rule: let R = |DOSE_00 - DOSE_00B| on the primary metric.  A dose is called better or worse only if it differs from DOSE_00 by more than R.  If DOSE_24 and DOSE_48 are both worse by more than R, rotating cut cells costs more than it buys at this budget and the historical --augment-full-only choice was right for the wrong reason.  If the ordering is monotone the other way, every cut arm so far has been leaving the one measured generalisation lever unused.  A result inside R is reported as unresolved at this budget, not as a null.
forbidden: reading the held-out set before the arms finish
changing the pool or the metric after seeing any arm

decode.why: the only chunk measured to reproduce the reference element for element; 32768 differs by 6.2e-7 relative on the factor
